scenes.tts: How can the same light touch recruit a pain pathway without changing the skin stimulus? Watch one blue touch signal enter the dorsal horn. It meets an orange relay, a purple inhibitory brake, and a red output route.
scenes.visual: Fill the frame with one labelled schematic mouse dorsal-horn cross-section. A blue pulse travels from skin into the cord. Orange relay, purple inhibitory neuron and red projection neuron grow from the pulse's path. Keep the pulse moving. On-screen label: 'mouse circuit, schematic'.
scenes.narration: How can the same light touch recruit a pain pathway without changing the skin stimulus? Watch one blue touch signal enter the dorsal horn. It meets an orange relay, a purple inhibitory brake, and a red output route.

scenes.visual: Keep the circuit moving slowly. The blue pulse loops at the entry while the title 'Who Opens the Touch Gate?' forms above it, then clears.

scenes.tts: First test the relay. In mice, removing the mostly excitatory somatostatin lineage weakens acute and injury-associated mechanical nocifensive behaviour. The result supports a relay role in the assays tested. It does not identify every route for mechanical pain.
scenes.visual: Carry the same circuit. Lift the orange relay out of the path. The red gauge, labelled 'nocifensive behaviour', falls while the blue input stays identical. A small card slides in: 'ablation: population removed'. Keep that gauge trembling.
scenes.narration: First test the relay. In mice, removing the mostly excitatory somatostatin lineage weakens acute and injury-associated mechanical nocifensive behaviour. The result supports a relay role in the assays tested. It does not identify every route for mechanical pain.

scenes.tts: Now restore the relay and test its brake. Dynorphin-lineage inhibitory neurons restrict recruitment of superficial somatostatin neurons by large myelinated afferents. The blue input is unchanged. Removing purple inhibition lets that input recruit many more orange cells.
scenes.visual: Return the orange relay. Purple inhibition visibly presses a brake bar across the blue-to-orange connection. Remove the purple cell and brake together. Additional orange cells illuminate from deep to superficial dorsal horn while blue input amplitude remains fixed.
scenes.narration: Now restore the relay and test its brake. Dynorphin-lineage inhibitory neurons restrict recruitment of superficial somatostatin neurons by large myelinated afferents. The blue input is unchanged. Removing purple inhibition lets that input recruit many more orange cells.

scenes.tts: Predict the slice result. With the inhibitory population removed, does identical A beta input recruit fewer superficial somatostatin cells, the same number, or more? Keep the incoming pulse fixed while you decide.
scenes.caption: Predict the slice result. With the inhibitory population removed, does identical Aβ input recruit fewer superficial somatostatin cells, the same number, or more? Keep the incoming pulse fixed while you decide.
scenes.visual: Show the carried circuit with the purple brake absent. Place three large choices beside the orange cells: 'fewer', 'same', 'more'. The blue pulse repeats at constant size. Do not reveal the answer.
scenes.narration: Predict the slice result. With the inhibitory population removed, does identical Aβ input recruit fewer superficial somatostatin cells, the same number, or more? Keep the incoming pulse fixed while you decide.

scenes.visual: Hold the predict question and three choices. The blue pulse continues moving every second. A thin thinking timer drains for four and a half seconds.

scenes.tts: More. At the lamina two to three border, A beta evoked spiking rose from five to forty percent of recorded neurons. The measurement locates a gated connection. The behaviour alone could not tell us where the circuit failed.
scenes.caption: More. At the lamina II–III border, Aβ-evoked spiking rose from 5% to 40% of recorded neurons. The measurement locates a gated connection. The behaviour alone could not tell us where the circuit failed.
scenes.visual: Transform the choices into one highlighted 'more'. Build a twenty-icon grid labelled 'percent of recorded neurons (schematic)': one icon lit for 5%, then eight for 40%, with the measured samples written small beside it as '2 of 38' and '12 of 30'. Keep 'mouse slice' visible.
scenes.narration: More. At the lamina II–III border, Aβ-evoked spiking rose from 5% to 40% of recorded neurons. The measurement locates a gated connection. The behaviour alone could not tell us where the circuit failed.

scenes.tts: Tools set the claim. Ablation removes captured cells, including cells marked by earlier expression. Tetanus toxin light chain can leave a neuron alive while blocking transmitter release. Activation asks whether added output can shift the measured behaviour.
scenes.visual: Carry one purple neuron into a three-position tool track. At 'ablation' the whole cell disappears. At 'silencing' the cell remains while transmitter dots stop. At 'activation' its output pulses strengthen. The orange relay and red output respond continuously.
scenes.narration: Tools set the claim. Ablation removes captured cells, including cells marked by earlier expression. Tetanus toxin light chain can leave a neuron alive while blocking transmitter release. Activation asks whether added output can shift the measured behaviour.

scenes.tts: Opposite manipulations sharpen the relay claim. Somatostatin activation elicited nocifensive behaviour. Inhibition raised mechanical withdrawal thresholds and lengthened thermal withdrawal latency in naive mice. Slice recordings confirmed that the light-driven neurons followed the stimulus trains.
scenes.visual: Carry the orange relay through an activation toggle and an inhibition toggle. Red nocifensive output rises with activation; mechanical and thermal response gauges fall with inhibition. Add a small slice inset where orange spikes follow repeated blue light pulses.
scenes.narration: Opposite manipulations sharpen the relay claim. Somatostatin activation elicited nocifensive behaviour. Inhibition raised mechanical withdrawal thresholds and lengthened thermal withdrawal latency in naive mice. Slice recordings confirmed that the light-driven neurons followed the stimulus trains.

scenes.tts: After spared nerve injury, permanent reporter counts of parvalbumin neurons did not fall significantly at three, five, or eight weeks. Yet activating those neurons relieved injury-associated hypersensitivity. The cells remained. The next question is what happened to their signal.
scenes.caption: After spared nerve injury, permanent reporter counts of parvalbumin neurons did not fall significantly at 3, 5, or 8 weeks. Yet activating those neurons relieved injury-associated hypersensitivity. The cells remained. The next question is what happened to their signal.
scenes.visual: Carry the purple parvalbumin neuron across a three-point timeline labelled 3, 5 and 8 weeks. Its count stays level. Then strengthen its purple output and lower the red hypersensitivity gauge. End with a question mark moving from the cell to its synapse.
scenes.narration: After spared nerve injury, permanent reporter counts of parvalbumin neurons did not fall significantly at 3, 5, or 8 weeks. Yet activating those neurons relieved injury-associated hypersensitivity. The cells remained. The next question is what happened to their signal.

scenes.tts: Inhibitory populations are not interchangeable. Parvalbumin activation changed mechanical sensitivity without changing thermal sensitivity in the assays tested. Broader glycinergic manipulations changed mechanical, heat, and cold sensitivity together. One gate does not control every modality.
scenes.visual: Split the carried output gauge into three large lanes: mechanical, heat and cold. Purple parvalbumin control moves only the mechanical lane. A wider purple glycinergic control moves all three. Label both panels 'mouse assays'.
scenes.narration: Inhibitory populations are not interchangeable. Parvalbumin activation changed mechanical sensitivity without changing thermal sensitivity in the assays tested. Broader glycinergic manipulations changed mechanical, heat, and cold sensitivity together. One gate does not control every modality.

scenes.tts: So begin with behaviour, but do not stop there. Ask which cells were captured, what the tool changed, and which connection was measured. Behaviour identifies a failed gate. Circuit measurements help locate the failure.
scenes.visual: Reassemble the original dorsal-horn circuit. Three questions orbit it: 'which cells?', 'which tool?', 'which connection?'. Each question locks onto the matching coloured object. The final red output arrow settles without freezing.
scenes.narration: So begin with behaviour, but do not stop there. Ask which cells were captured, what the tool changed, and which connection was measured. Behaviour identifies a failed gate. Circuit measurements help locate the failure.

scenes.visual: End card over the slowly pulsing circuit: 'Match behaviour to the tool and the circuit.' Keep the eight-word line large and centered.
